summary:
I re-ran this lens on the current build (master tip 1d176f8a + working tree). The run was a RIFT bot match on the render bench at 1080p High, on the real Chrome GPU, with waves frozen and bots muted on the mid-lane stone at (74, 55). I used my own scripts (_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify_tools/verify*.mjs, logs run*.log) and wrote the reports to _harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json, final_combat_verify2.json and final_combat_verify3.json.

The blocker reproduces exactly:
- Every cone indicator is filled inside-out, both enemy warnings and own aim.
- Across 31 frames of Tunlan's ultimate, seen from the enemy side, the cone axis stays at alpha 0 while the safe ground behind the apex fills.
- For own aim (Ardit a2, Vashil a3, Ervet a1), the axis is at 0 and the area beside and behind is at 31.
- The sign error is at telegraphs.ts:76.

These also reproduce:
- Recall shows its effect for only about the first second (F2).
- 3 of 4 ultimates I tested re-fire the full exposure beat every 1 s (F3).
- Some kits lose their signature hue in play (F6).

Two findings were overstated:
- F4's headline claim, that the ultimate misses LoL's brightness, is a measurement artifact. Inside the lit core on lane stone the peak is 2.27–2.64×, which meets LoL's 2.3–2.5×. The reviewer's 1.55–2.17× was a mean over a duel box much larger than the ≤ 3.5 m lift. What is left of F4 (victim whiteout for 2–3 frames, lift anchored on the caster for Tunlan's cone and Rishal's rect) is minor.
- F5 is minor. The overhead CC strip already appears only for hard CC and drains by remaining/duration (renderer.ts:148, :814). The CC looks last their full duration for all 17 kinds. Only the word and icon are missing.

The score stays at 6: one S-size blocker plus three majors.

gapStatus.evidence:
Reproduced. Circles, rings and rects draw. Every cone draws inverted.

Enemy view (final_combat_verify.json `cone`, Tunlan ult seen by team 0, f1–f31):
- Samples on the axis at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 r read alpha 0 in every frame.
- Total telegraph pixels grow from 9.3k to 188k.
- The point 0.4 m behind the apex fills to alpha 43–102.
- Shot: _harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_cone_tunlan_ult_f20.jpg.

Own aim (`aim`): Ardit a2, Vashil a3 and Ervet a1 read 0 on the axis and 31 beside, outside and behind the apex (_harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_aim_ardit_a2.jpg).

Cause: src/render/overlay/telegraphs.ts:76.

Content check: all 13 delayed damaging areas are telegraph:'everyone', and each has castTime + delay ≥ 0.60 s (smallest: Vashil a1 0.2+0.4, Dunsom a1 0.25+0.4). This agrees with the reviewer's lead times. The cone fill error is a B2 problem, not an M1 one.

In place:
- Looks are sustained for all 17 kinds (reviewer, _harness/_shots/final_combat_cc_status_looks.png).
- The bar already has a hard-CC-only strip that drains by remaining/duration (src/render/renderer.ts:148 HARD_CC, :814), so hard CC does read stronger than damage.

Missing: the word and icon above the bar. tokens hud.overheadBar.statusIconPx and maxStatusIcons have no consumer, and bars.ts:194-200 draws the strip only.
Re-counted from content: 48 of 48 casts with castTime ≥ 0.12 s have a windupVfx def that exists in content/vfx.json.

Re-computed attack.windup / base.attackSpeed:
- Ranged: 0.309–0.375 s.
- Melee: Nurrow 0.373, Rishal 0.368, Ardit 0.406, Ervet 0.415, Kemdo 0.415, Marund 0.422, Burdam 0.424, Hesmi 0.452 s.

Six of eight melee fighters are above LoL's 0.40 s. Impact hold and Hesmi's pose are per the reviewer's pose probe (not re-measured).
Not re-measured beyond the ultimate runs. The struck victim lit in every ultimate test (victim box mean luma 94 → 226–239 at the beat). The reviewer's flash series (0.7 → 0 by frame 5) stands.

Content meets r12's M12 spec (my count over content/vfx.json):
- Signature is 56–80 % of each kit's emissive layers.
- Team colour is 8–26 % of them.
- The reviewer's 39 % team share for Tunlan was not reproduced.

In play the signature survives for only about half the slots. I measured the hue of the light the VFX add (positive on-minus-off delta, telegraph layer hidden), as the share of saturated pixels within ±25° of the signature (final_combat_verify3.json `hue`):
- Strong: Lisvel 0.92/0.75, Burdam 0.90/0.94, Kemdo 0.96/0.78, Dunsom a2 0.76, Vashil a2 0.61.
- Lost: Tunlan 0.04/0.08, Rishal 0.11/0.00 (reads blue, 210–240°), Hesmi a2 0.01.
- Odrum 0.43/0.41, with 68–91 % of pixels in the HARM band 20–55°.

Brightness is at the gauge. Core (0.5× lift radius) luma base → peak on lane stone (final_combat_verify.json `ult`):
- Kemdo 97.4 → 234 (2.41×).
- Rishal 92.1 → 219–243 (2.38–2.64×).
- Tunlan 95.8 → 218–222 (2.27–2.32×).
- Hesmi 93.3 → 226 (2.42×).

Still open:
- Re-firing beats: Kemdo at 0.30/1.30/2.30 s, Rishal 0.23/1.23/2.23 s, Hesmi 1.17/2.13/3.13 s. Tunlan fires once.
- The lift is anchored on the caster for Tunlan's cone and Rishal's rect.
- Victim whiteout for 2–3 frames.
Camera displacement was 0.0000 in all 4 of my ultimate runs (`ult[].camJitter`). content/vfx.json has 0 feel layers with shake > 0.
33 defs carry a distort layer by my count (the reviewer says 34; this does not change the status).
Death grade per the reviewer (not re-measured). Recall arrival, level-up and kill banners were not measured by either pass.

findings.title: Every cone telegraph and cone aim indicator is drawn inside-out
findings.what:
`sdSector` keeps the side test from Inigo Quilez's +y-axis sector SDF after re-axing the shape to +x. Points inside the half-angle therefore come out positive (outside), and points beside or behind the apex come out negative (inside).

As a result, the fill, the landing flash and the sweep paint the safe ground beside and behind the caster, and leave the real cone empty. Only the two radial edge lines are right.

Affected: Ardit a2, Burdam a3, Ervet a1, Tunlan ult (an enemy-visible 9 m fear) and Vashil a3, in both enemy warnings and own aim.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced on the current build:

Enemy view: _harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json `cone`, Tunlan ult seen by team 0.
- In all 31 frames, the samples on the axis at 0.25, 0.5 and 0.75 r read alpha 0.
- Total telegraph pixels grow from 9.3k to 188k.
- The point 0.4 m behind the apex reads 43 → 102.
- Shots: _harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_cone_tunlan_ult_f9.jpg and _f20.jpg.

Own aim (`aim`, via renderer.setAim):
- Ardit a2, Vashil a3 and Ervet a1: axis 0/0/0, beside ±90° 31, outside the angle 31, behind 31.
- Shot: _harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_aim_ardit_a2.jpg.

Math (src/render/overlay/telegraphs.ts:76, `m * sign(c.y*p.x - c.x*p.y)` with c = (cos ha, sin ha)):
- r 9, ha 25°: p = (4.5, 0) gives d = +1.90 (outside), and p = (−4, 0) gives d = −4.00 (inside).
- The correct +x form is `sign(c.x*p.y - c.y*p.x)`.

_harness/overlay_regress.mjs has no cone case.

Repro:
```
node _harness/_reports/final_combat_verify_tools/verify.mjs cone,aim
```
findings.gauge: LoL (r12 B2, R1): an indicator fills exactly the area that will be hit, with a translucent fill and a bright rim. It never paints safe ground.
findings.fix:
1. In sdSector, use `m * sign(c.x*p.y - c.y*p.x)` (after `p.y = abs(p.y)`).
2. Add a cone case to overlay_regress, for both the enemy telegraph and the own aim:
   - the pixel on the axis at r/2 must be filled;
   - the pixels at 90° and 0.4 m behind the apex must be empty.
3. Re-shoot Tunlan's ultimate from the enemy side.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced with independent pixel sampling on both the enemy and own paths, and the math checks out. Blocker severity is kept: the bug inverts the meaning of the primary danger cue for 5 abilities, including an enemy-visible ultimate. The fix is a one-line sign change.

findings.title: Recall effect is visible for about 1 s of a ≈ 6.9 s channel
findings.what: lib_recall is a 1.0 s def that the director fires once, at start and again at done, with no sustain. For the rest of the channel nothing but the body clip shows that the unit is recalling: no effect and no bar cue.
findings.evidence:
_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify2.json `recall`: ally Odrum recalling alone, seen by team 0. Pixels added by the VFX inside a 240 px box:
- 0.1 s: 5,302.
- 0.5 s: 5,925.
- 1.0 s: 152.
- 1.5 s: 21.
- 2.0 s: 0.
- 3.0 s: 19.
- 5.0 s: 0.
- 6.7 s: 0.
- 'done' at f206 (6.87 s): 8,059 (departure).

The actor plays its 'recall' clip throughout (a kneel), so the unit does not look exactly idle as the reviewer said. Even so, no effect is visible from 1.5 s on (_harness/_shots/final_combat_verify_recall_ally_f090.jpg, f150).

Code: src/render/director.ts:597-604 fires with no sustain or loopWhile. content/vfx.json lib_recall has duration 1.0, and its comment says '(loop)'.
findings.gauge: LoL: a recall is a clearly visible, team-coloured channel for its whole duration. Any enemy with vision reads it, and the channel is also shown on the health bar. It ends in a departure flash.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced with an ally recall that was not interrupted (my first enemy-recall attempt was cancelled by an auto-attack at 1 s). One correction: the body does play a dedicated recall clip. Major is right, because the state is invisible as an effect for about 80 % of the channel.

findings.title: Ultimates that hit repeatedly re-fire the full exposure beat about every second
findings.what: Every T4 `hit` event queues an exposure pulse. The only limit is a 0.6 s gate per caster, so an ultimate that ticks or hits again fires a fresh ×2.4 beat roughly every second, for as long as it lasts. This contradicts the code's own comment, 'a targeted ultimate's first hit carries the impact envelope'.
findings.evidence:
_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json `ult[].liftStarts`, start times of lifts ≥ 1.3:
- Kemdo: 0.30, 1.30 and 2.30 s. Hits fall every 0.5 s (f8, 23, 38, 53, 68, 83), so every second hit pulses.
- Rishal: 0.23, 1.23 and 2.23 s.
- Hesmi: 1.17, 2.13 and 3.13 s.
- Tunlan: 0.93 s only.

The later beats centre on the victim and whiten 59–60 % of its box pixels (`peaks`).

Code: src/render/director.ts:443-444 (hit case), with the gate at :374-377.

The reviewer's photosensitivity framing is overstated: one ultimate pulses at 1 Hz, below the 3 flashes/s guideline.
findings.gauge: r12 M13 (V4, V5): one envelope of about 1 s per ultimate impact. Lingering effects never re-flash.
findings.fix:
1. Key the envelope to the cast instance: (src, ability, cast time). Once that cast's first area, hit or zone has pulsed, ignore further pulses from it.
2. Let a def opt in to repeated beats explicitly (Vashil's tolls), at a reduced peak.
findings.verifierNote: Reproduced on 3 of the 4 ultimates I ran. Major is kept: half of the ultimates misrepresent their impact and pulse the frame repeatedly in fights. The fix is small.

findings.title: Ultimate beat whites out the struck unit for 2–3 frames and is anchored on the caster for caster-origin cones and rects
findings.what:
The headline claim, that the peak misses LoL's brightness on lane stone, does not hold. Inside the lit core the peak is 2.27–2.64×, so the brightness meets the gauge.

What remains:
- At each beat the struck unit goes mostly white for 2–3 frames.
- Tunlan's cone ultimate and Rishal's rect ultimate centre the lift on the caster instead of on the area that hits.
findings.evidence:
_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify.json `ult`. Core = a circle of 0.5× the lift radius around the uLiftA centre, same camera.

Peak brightness, base → peak:
- Kemdo: 97.4 → 234.3 (2.41×).
- Rishal: 92.1 → 219–243 (2.38–2.64×).
- Tunlan: 95.8 → 218–222 (2.27–2.32×).
- Hesmi: 93.3 → 226 (2.42×).
- The reviewer's 1.55–2.17× was the mean of a ~700×400 px duel box, larger than the ≤ 3.5 m lift (PULSE_MAX_R, director.ts:155), so the ratio was diluted.

Whiteout, share of white pixels in the victim box:
- Base: 2–5 %.
- First beat: 22–34 % (Kemdo, Hesmi).
- Re-fired beats: 59–60 %.
- The lift reaches ≥ 1.3 for only 2–3 frames.

Anchor (`ult[].firstCtr`):
- Tunlan: lift at [774, 519], caster at [775, 540], victim at [1145, 540].
- Rishal's rect: the same, on the caster.
- Kemdo and Hesmi: correctly on the victim.

Shot: _harness/_shots/final_combat_ult_peak_frames.png (reviewer).
findings.gauge: r12 M13: one frame at 2.3–2.5× fight-area brightness. This is met in the core. R1: never full-screen white, and champions stay readable. LoL's own hit flash on champions lasts 1–2 frames.
findings.fix:
1. Anchor the pulse at the shape's centroid: a cone at origin + dir·0.6r, a rect at origin + dir·L/2. The director's area case currently takes ev.x/ev.y when the area matches a zone.
2. Cap the lift on actor pixels at about ×1.3 so struck units keep their silhouette.
3. F3 removes the 59–60 % whiteouts on re-fired beats.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major to minor. The brightness part is a measurement artifact: the core meets 2.3–2.5×. The first-beat whiteout of 2–3 frames is close to LoL's 1–2-frame hit flash. The caster anchor is real but affects 2 ultimates. The new evidence shows the anchor issue also affects Rishal's rect, not only Tunlan's cone.

findings.title: Crowd control has no word or icon on the overhead bar
findings.what: All 17 CC kinds show an in-world look for their full duration. The overhead bar also shows a strip, only for hard CC, that drains by remaining/duration. What is missing is the status word or glyph above an affected unit's bar, which LoL shows.
findings.evidence:
Present:
- src/render/renderer.ts:148 defines HARD_CC (stun, root, airborne, taunt, fear, sleep, silence).
- renderer.ts:814 sets the strip to remaining/duration for hard CC only, and bars.ts:194-200 draws it.
- So hard CC already reads stronger than damage on the bar, and the reviewer's fix step 3 already exists.

Missing:
- _design/tokens.json hud.overheadBar statusIconPx 14 / maxStatusIcons 3 have no consumer in src/.
- status.<kind>.name is used only by the HUD self chip (src/ui/hud/status.tsx:164) and the ability lock (dialbar.tsx:291).
- No word appears in _harness/_shots/final_combat_cc_status_looks.png.
findings.gauge: r12 M2 (V5, R7, R8): words such as STUNNED or AIRBORNE above the bars, readable in 6–10-effect teamfights. The primary CC read in LoL is still the in-world effect, which VALE now has.
findings.fix: Add a CC plate to the BarLayer label atlas: the StatusGlyph at 14 px and the status name in caps at 12–13 px with an ink outline, highest-priority hard CC only, fading in over 70 ms. The existing drain strip stays.
findings.verifierNote: Downgraded from major to minor. The main gap behind M2 (invisible or one-shot CC) is closed, and a hard-CC duration strip already exists. Only the word or icon is missing.

findings.title: Several kits lose their signature hue in play (Tunlan, Rishal, Hesmi a2) and Odrum sits in the enemy HARM band
findings.what:
Content now follows r12's M12 spec:
- Signature is ≥ 50 % of each kit's emissive layers.
- Team colour is ≤ 26 % of them.
- Same-hue pairs pass the documented ΔL* ≥ 25 rule.

In play, though, the light some kits add is mostly white, blue or warm orange rather than their signature. About half of the a1/a2 slots are identifiable by hue alone.
findings.evidence:
_harness/_reports/final_combat_verify3.json `hue`. Metric: the hue of the light the VFX add (positive VFX-on minus VFX-off delta, telegraph layer hidden), measured a few frames after release, as the share of saturated pixels within ±25° of the signature.

Strong:
- Lisvel 0.92 / 0.75.
- Burdam 0.90 / 0.94.
- Kemdo 0.96 / 0.78, though its salmon H13 sits next to HARM: 45 % of a1 pixels are in 20–55°.
- Dunsom a2 0.76.
- Vashil a2 0.61.

Lost:
- Tunlan 0.04 / 0.08 (a1 is 61 % white).
- Rishal 0.11 / 0.00: dominant hue 210–240°, blue, not orange as the reviewer said.
- Hesmi a2 0.01 (78 % white).
- Odrum 0.43 / 0.41, with 68–91 % of saturated pixels in the HARM band.

Layer shares (my count over content/vfx.json, emissive layers): signature 56–80 %, team 8–26 %. The reviewer's 'Tunlan 42 % / 39 %' was not reproduced.

Contact sheet: _harness/_shots/final_combat_identity_a1_a2.png (reviewer).
findings.gauge: r12 M12 (C1, R1): every champion owns a signature hue that survives in play. Hit sparks share a warm white, and team colour lives in indicators, rings and rims.
findings.fix:
1. Re-tune the cores of Tunlan, Rishal, Hesmi and Odrum so the signature survives tone mapping and bloom:
   - cap core luminance after tone mapping at about 0.85;
   - saturation ≥ 0.45;
   - give each a signature motif shape.
2. Move Odrum's signature at least 15° further from the HARM band, or give it a cool secondary in the core.
3. Add a vfx_gallery or bench check that reports each kit's in-play signature share using this additive-delta metric, with a gate of ≥ 0.5 per slot.
4. The same-hue pairs are allowed by the documented rule, so they need no change by themselves.
findings.verifierNote:
Confirmed as major, by measurement rather than a contact sheet. The specifics differ from the review:
- Hesmi is not reliably violet.
- Rishal reads blue, not orange.
- Content layer shares already meet the spec.
- The same-hue-pair complaint is a design choice the docs allow.

The gap, that signatures do not survive in play for about a quarter to half of the slots, is real.

findings.title: Basic-attack impacts fade in about 100 ms, and six melee wind-ups are above 0.40 s
findings.what: The impact element is large on its first frame and mostly gone by 133 ms. Six of the eight melee wind-ups are 0.406–0.452 s.
findings.evidence: Re-computed content/fighters/*.json attack.windup / base.attackSpeed: Ardit 0.406, Ervet 0.415, Kemdo 0.415, Marund 0.422, Burdam 0.424, Hesmi 0.452 s. Impact decay per the reviewer's _harness/_reports/final_combat_attack_pose.json (not re-measured).
findings.gauge: r12 M5 (C1, V4): wind-up 250–400 ms; an impact starburst of ≈ 0.7× victim height for ≈ 200 ms.
findings.fix:
1. Hold a mid-scale impact element at full for 2 frames, then ease it out over 160–200 ms.
2. Trim the heavy melee wind-ups toward 0.36–0.40 s.
3. Re-run the balance sims.

findings.title: Hesmi's basic attack has little body motion
findings.what: The weapon tip travels 0.61 m over a 13-frame wind-up, against about 3 m for Kemdo and Marund.
findings.gauge: r12 M5: three readable poses; the weapon tip travels ≥ 0.6× champion height.

findings.title: Large-area landing flashes wash the frame orange at impact
findings.what: At landing, the telegraph fill rises to 40 % over the whole shape for 150 ms, on top of the exposure lift.
findings.evidence: src/render/renderer.ts:861 `spec.fill = flash ? 0.4 : …`. Burdam ult f14 in _harness/_shots/final_combat_ult_peak_frames.png.
findings.gauge: r12 B2 / R1: the warning yields to the impact and never becomes a flat wash.
findings.fix: On areas over 4 m radius, flash only the edge band and an inner ring, with fill ≤ 0.22.
